subject: Spatial field looks very different after rerunnning model

messages.author: d1d50f3a3afe11e3
messages.subject: Spatial field looks very different after rerunnning model
parts:
Dear all,

I am quite new to R-INLA and struggling with the following problem: After I reran my spde R-INLA model on a different computer the resulting spatial fields looked strikingly different.

Version A looks quite smooth and the range of the correlation ranges relatively far, while Version B is much more patchy with a shorter correlation range (see attatched figures).
(In between I also ended up with a third Version C, where even the direction of the deviations looked different.)
My first guess was that I somehow accidentally made a tipo somewhere in the Code and changed, e.g. the priors of the spde without intending to.
However, playing around with different priors did not change the output very much. I also tried different meshes (e.g. with a RangeGuess of 100, 200 and 300 km) in a "fresh" R-Project.
I now consistently end up with (slightly differing) "Version B" and I haven't been able to reproduce the "Version A spatial field".

from inla.emarginal() I got:
Version A: kappa = 4.67 e-06, sigma_u = 4.01, range = 608 km
Version B: kappa = 5.37 e-05, sigma_u = 10.69, range = 59 km

I would be super gratful for any hints on what I must be overlooking that explains the different outcomes.

Thanks a lot!

Best,
Franziska

Below is the code I used:

# Make mesh

RangeGuess100 <- 100 * 1000                                    
MaxEdge100 <- RangeGuess100 / 5
mesh100 <- inla.mesh.2d(Loc.ce,                                 # UTM coordinates (using latitude and longitude instead produces nearly identical results)
                       max.edge = c(1, 5) * MaxEdge100,         # range is in km and maximum distance is around 3000km     
                       cutoff = MaxEdge100 / 5)

# Make spde
spde100 <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh100,
                             prior.range = c(100 * 1000, 0.5),  # I changed the priors here e.g. by changing 100 to 500 or 0.5 to 0.05
                             prior.sigma = c(35, 0.05))         # I also tried different priors here, e.g. (10, 0.05), [35 = variance in Null-Model, summary(lm(DOY ~ 1, data = D.ce))$sigma]

# Define the spatial field.
w100 <- inla.spde.make.index('w', n.spde = spde100$n.spde)

# Make Stack
Stack100 <- inla.stack(
            tag = "Fit",
            data = list(y = D.ce$DOY),                         # Response variable = "day of the year" (ranges from 50-200)
              A = list(1, 1, A100, 1, A_rs),   
              effects = list(  
                  Intercept = rep(1, N.ce),
                  X = X.all,                                   # Matrix with covariates
                  w = w100,                                    # Spatial component from spde
                  Species = D.ce$Species,           
                  Species2 = D.ce$Species          
                  ))

# Model formula
priorpc <- list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(35, 0.05)))

f <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + various_Covariates +
        f(Species, model = "iid", hyper = priorpc) +          # random intercept for species
        f(Species2, model = "iid", hyper = priorpc) +         # random slopes for species
        f(w, model = spde100test)

# Run model
Model100 <- inla(f,
                   family = "gaussian", 
                   data=inla.stack.data(Stack100),
                   control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
                   control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(Stack100)))

# Spatial field
w.pm.100 <- Model100$summary.random$w$mean

# Plot spatial field
PlotField(field = w.pm.100, mesh = mesh100, ContourMap = Eu.UTM, xlim = c(-1001008,1960055)) # modified code from material on Haakon Bakka's website

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial field looks very different after rerunnning model
parts:
Hi,

the xlim in the plot appears to still be in metres?  One thing to double check that all your data has been correctly converted to kilometres.
But it looks like you may be in a model situation that is poorly identified in a way that is numerically unstable.
What INLA versions were used for the two runs? The default value for the numerical gradient step size was recently changed to make it more stable.
You can set it with control.inla = list(h=0.005) on older versions (the old default was h=0.01).
Also try using inla.rerun() to improve the estimate in case the numerics is the issue.
Showing the full model summaries may also be helpful.

Finn

Am Mittwoch, 30. September 2020 16:05:06 UTC+2 schrieb Finn Lindgren:

Hi,

the xlim in the plot appears to still be in metres?  One thing to double check that all your data has been correctly converted to kilometres.
But it looks like you may be in a model situation that is poorly identified in a way that is numerically unstable.
What INLA versions were used for the two runs? The default value for the numerical gradient step size was recently changed to make it more stable.
You can set it with control.inla = list(h=0.005) on older versions (the old default was h=0.01).
Also try using inla.rerun() to improve the estimate in case the numerics is the issue.
Showing the full model summaries may also be helpful.

Finn

Dear all,

I am quite new to R-INLA and struggling with the following problem: After I reran my spde R-INLA model on a different computer the resulting spatial fields looked strikingly different.

Version A looks quite smooth and the range of the correlation ranges relatively far, while Version B is much more patchy with a shorter correlation range (see attatched figures).
(In between I also ended up with a third Version C, where even the direction of the deviations looked different.)
My first guess was that I somehow accidentally made a tipo somewhere in the Code and changed, e.g. the priors of the spde without intending to.
However, playing around with different priors did not change the output very much. I also tried different meshes (e.g. with a RangeGuess of 100, 200 and 300 km) in a "fresh" R-Project.
I now consistently end up with (slightly differing) "Version B" and I haven't been able to reproduce the "Version A spatial field".

from inla.emarginal() I got:
Version A: kappa = 4.67 e-06, sigma_u = 4.01, range = 608 km
Version B: kappa = 5.37 e-05, sigma_u = 10.69, range = 59 km

I would be super gratful for any hints on what I must be overlooking that explains the different outcomes.

Thanks a lot!

Best,
Franziska

Below is the code I used:

# Make mesh

RangeGuess100 <- 100 * 1000                                    
MaxEdge100 <- RangeGuess100 / 5
mesh100 <- inla.mesh.2d(Loc.ce,                                 # UTM coordinates (using latitude and longitude instead produces nearly identical results)
                       max.edge = c(1, 5) * MaxEdge100,         # range is in km and maximum distance is around 3000km     
                       cutoff = MaxEdge100 / 5)

# Make spde
spde100 <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh100,
                             prior.range = c(100 * 1000, 0.5),  # I changed the priors here e.g. by changing 100 to 500 or 0.5 to 0.05
                             prior.sigma = c(35, 0.05))         # I also tried different priors here, e.g. (10, 0.05), [35 = variance in Null-Model, summary(lm(DOY ~ 1, data = D.ce))$sigma]

# Define the spatial field.
w100 <- inla.spde.make.index('w', n.spde = spde100$n.spde)

# Make Stack
Stack100 <- inla.stack(
            tag = "Fit",
            data = list(y = D.ce$DOY),                         # Response variable = "day of the year" (ranges from 50-200)
              A = list(1, 1, A100, 1, A_rs),   
              effects = list(  
                  Intercept = rep(1, N.ce),
                  X = X.all,                                   # Matrix with covariates
                  w = w100,                                    # Spatial component from spde
                  Species = D.ce$Species,           
                  Species2 = D.ce$Species          
                  ))

# Model formula
priorpc <- list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(35, 0.05)))

f <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + various_Covariates +
        f(Species, model = "iid", hyper = priorpc) +          # random intercept for species
        f(Species2, model = "iid", hyper = priorpc) +         # random slopes for species
        f(w, model = spde100test)

# Run model
Model100 <- inla(f,
                   family = "gaussian", 
                   data=inla.stack.data(Stack100),
                   control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE),
                   control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(Stack100)))

# Spatial field
w.pm.100 <- Model100$summary.random$w$mean

# Plot spatial field
PlotField(field = w.pm.100, mesh = mesh100, ContourMap = Eu.UTM, xlim = c(-1001008,1960055)) # modified code from material on Haakon Bakka's website
